terms.gloss: a form of a word, an inflected form
evidence: Quint. 1.4.29: quaedam tertiae dēmum persōnae figūrā dīcuntur ut licet, piget (Lewis & Short)
Varr. LL 9.52; 9.55 (Lewis & Short: “form of a word, inflection”)
terms.comment: The shape a word takes in inflection: give the plural form of gaudium, dā (dīc) figūram plūrālem «gaudium» nōminis (Traupman 246). A form is simple or compound: figūra est aut simplex, ut «doctus», aut composita, ut «indoctus» (Traupman 246). To form the imperative is facere imperātīvum (Traupman 246).

phrases.latin: quaedam tertiae dēmum persōnae figūrā dīcuntur ut licet, piget
phrases.english: some are said only in the form of the third person, as licet, piget

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 225, p. 230, p. 246.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
